attribution.note: Zitron's own first-person words in his own newsletter post, published under his name.

semantics.note: Firm present-tense observation with two parts: the typical build time for data centers above 50MW, and the absence of any completed gigawatt facility. The normalisation leaves out 'across the board' and 'or lower, in some cases', but these do not change the core commitment.

contract.note: The plain reading is fair and ordinary: the range describes typical full-project builds, and 'built' means a completed facility of at least 1GW by May 12, 2026. The result depends on which project boundary and power definition are used (IT versus total facility power), and the speaker supplied neither.

evidence.note: JLL's 2026 outlook gives an 18-month average for a 50MW build. This matches the bottom of the claimed range but covers only one size point and is not a distribution of build times for projects above 50MW.

Musk's January 2026 announcement that the first gigawatt cluster was operational is a company statement about itself. It gives no capacity definition and no commissioning record, and Epoch's later reconstruction qualifies it, so it cannot independently contradict the claim.

Epoch's satellite reconstruction estimates about 490MW of IT power at Colossus 2 on April 6, 2026, with cooling still under construction. It does not establish 1GW completed by May 12, nor does it prove that no gigawatt facility existed anywhere in the world.
Epoch's methodology note separates reaching 1GW of facility power from completing a campus. It is useful for interpretation but says nothing direct about the outcome.

reviews.rationale: Neither part of the claim is settled. On build time, the only benchmark covers a 50MW project, so there is no representative record of builds above 50MW. On the gigawatt claim, xAI's assertion about Colossus 2 is self-reported, and Epoch's estimate of about 490MW of IT power in April does not show a completed gigawatt facility by May 12. No worldwide inventory proves none existed, and a lack of verified counterexamples does not count as support.
